evidence_c1: Recruitment frame and sampling strategy are not established in the reviewed sections.
evidence_c2: The outcome measures are described but the available report does not establish their appropriateness sufficiently.
evidence_c3: Completeness of outcome data and attrition are not established.
evidence_c4: Group allocation and baseline confounder control are not sufficiently documented.
evidence_c5: The article's introduction refers to one academic semester, methods report six weeks, and the results show week-eight progress for high-interaction programming students; this reporting conflict does not establish adherence or chronology for the mathematics component.

evidence_c1: A qualitative approach is relevant to examining student and educator perceptions of the tutoring system.
evidence_c2: Surveys and structured interviews are reported but participant selection and collection procedures need fuller support.
evidence_c3: Thematic analysis is named but the derivation of themes is not described in enough detail.
evidence_c4: Interpretation is not sufficiently substantiated by the qualitative material reported.
evidence_c5: Coherence between qualitative sources, collection, analysis, and interpretation remains unclear.

evidence_c1: The cohorts are from one course and separated by four years; the target population and selection process are not sufficiently described.
evidence_c2: Questionnaire and course outcomes are described and analyzed; the appraisal remains provisional.
evidence_c3: Completeness and disposition of outcome data are not sufficiently documented in the reviewed sections.
evidence_c4: The noncontemporaneous control and experimental cohorts create temporal confounding acknowledged by the authors.
evidence_c5: Intervention implementation and adherence are not documented sufficiently for this criterion.

evidence_c1: Interviews are appropriate to explore student perspectives on the course reform.
evidence_c2: The article reports semi-structured interviews with 12 students from the experimental cohort.
evidence_c3: The analytic steps used to derive themes are not sufficiently detailed.
evidence_c4: The interpretation includes student accounts and is supported by reported quotations.
evidence_c5: The relationship among qualitative sampling, collection, analysis, and integrated claims needs further verification.

evidence_c1: The one-school student records fit the local classification question described by the study.
evidence_c2: A broader target population and sampling frame are not sufficiently defined.
evidence_c3: Eight scale items used to construct the mindset categories also remain among selected predictors, compromising independent measurement of the target.
evidence_c4: The report gives 633 recruited and 428 complete cases and cites academic years 2023–2024 and 2022–2023 without clarifying cohort provenance or whether missing cases create nonresponse bias.
evidence_c5: The split and validation descriptions conflict and do not permit a clear appraisal of analysis appropriateness.

evidence_c1: Teacher interviews are relevant to the study's stated contextual and triangulation aims.
evidence_c2: The interview method is reported but selection and collection details are insufficiently documented.
evidence_c3: The analytic procedure for the interview material is not adequately described.
evidence_c4: Interpretation of the teacher interviews is not sufficiently substantiated in the reviewed report.
evidence_c5: Coherence among the student-record analysis, teacher interviews, collection, and interpretation needs further verification.
